title: Bangladesh garment workers’ council demands $260 minimum monthly wage
description:
IndustriALL Bangladesh Council has demanded a $260 monthly minimum wage for Bangladesh garment workers, citing higher living costs and market volatility.
IBC said essentials, transport and medical costs had strained workers, alongside a 100 to 142 per cent rise for government employees.
It plans grade-wise wage proposals once the full wage board is formed.

title: Apparel Sourcing and Garment Export Companies in Bangladesh
description:
Bangladesh has become one of the most trusted countries for apparel sourcing and garment exports. Global fashion brands choose Bangladesh because of its skilled workforce, competitive production cost, strong factory network, and growing focus on compliance and sustainability. According to Texasia, Bangladesh remains one of the leading destinations for brands looking for reliable garment production and export support.

The country is especially strong in knitwear, woven garments, denim, T-shirts, polo shirts, hoodies, jackets, trousers, kidswear, sportswear, and custom clothing production. Many apparel sourcing companies in Bangladesh also support buyers with fabric sourcing, sampling, quality control, export documentation, and shipment handling.

title: 229 eco-friendly garment factories in Bangladesh now: BGMEA
description: The number of LEED-certified green factories in Bangladesh is 229 now, after three more apparel and textile factories were recently certified by the US Green Building Council: Sepal Garments Ltd in Gazipur, Unitex Spinning Ltd (Unit-2) in Chattogram and Ananta Huaxiang Limited in Narayanganj. The country is now home to 61 of the top 100 highest-rated LEED certified factories in the world.

title: IAF launches manifesto for smart, sustainable apparel manufacturing
description:
IAF’s new manifesto urges apparel manufacturers and brands to move beyond lowest-cost sourcing and focus on end-to-end productivity, demand alignment and supply chain resilience. 
It highlights smart flexibility, stronger textile-apparel collaboration and lower inventory risk. 
The roadmap centres on defining shared goals, enabling innovation and standardising scalable industry practices.
